question.text: When a portfolio manager invests client funds in mutual fund units, which of the following is true under SEBI norms?

answer.text: The portfolio manager may invest through either direct or regular plans and may pass on distributor commissions to the client
The portfolio manager must invest only through direct plans of mutual fund schemes and may not charge any distribution-related fees
The portfolio manager may invest only through regular plans of mutual fund schemes
There are no restrictions on the type of mutual fund plan used by the portfolio manager

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that when portfolio managers invest client assets in mutual fund units, they must use the direct plan of the scheme and are not permitted to charge any distribution-related fees on such investments. The Trap: Options that allow regular plans or distributor commissions confuse the general retail MF distribution rules with the specific PMS rule. PMS clients are protected from a double layer of fees on the underlying MF leg. Note: Direct plans avoid distribution costs at the mutual fund level; the PMS fee structure (management, performance and operating expenses) is separately governed under the PMS regulations.
